findings.title: Invalid timestamp meanings escape the promised signal error
findings.description: `SignalEvent` promises that a timestamp whose meaning is not `AVAILABLE_AT` raises `InvalidSignalError`, but `Timestamp.__post_init__` only validates the nanosecond range and accepts an arbitrary `meaning` at runtime. When `SignalEvent` detects a mismatched meaning, it formats the error with `self.time.meaning.value`; a value such as `Timestamp(100, "available_at")` therefore raises `AttributeError` instead of `InvalidSignalError`. Validate the meaning type before comparing it, and add a regression test covering a malformed `Timestamp.meaning`.

findings.title: Integer coercion rounds fractional real values into integers
findings.description: For non-`Integral` values, `as_integer` first converts the value to a floating-point number and then checks `is_integer()`. This can silently change a fractional real into an integer: for example, `Fraction(10**100 + 1, 10**100)` converts to `1.0` and is accepted as `1`, despite not being integral. Because parameter declarations and binding use this function, such a value can enter a run parameter under a different value. Determine integrality from the original value before any lossy float conversion, or explicitly restrict the accepted non-integral types, and add regression coverage for a fractional `numbers.Real`.
